Two sequences \(a, a'\) give the same \(b\) exactly when their difference \(d = a - a'\) satisfies \(d_1+d_2=0\), \(d_{i-1}+d_i+d_{i+1}=0\) for \(1<i<20\), and \(d_{19}+d_{20}=0\), with every \(d_i \in \{-1,0,1\}\).

**Kernel.** The conditions force \(d_3=0\), \(d_4=d_1\), and so on, so \(d\) has period 3. Writing \(d_1=x\), we get \(d=(x,-x,0,x,-x,0,\ldots)\). Since \(20\equiv 2 \pmod 3\), the last two entries are \(d_{19}=x\) and \(d_{20}=-x\), which satisfy the end condition. So the nonzero kernel direction is \(d_0=(1,-1,0,1,-1,0,\ldots,1,-1)\), and the preimages of any \(b\) are the 0/1 vectors on a line \(a+t\,d_0\).

**Structure of \(a\).** The positions split into:
- 7 pairs \((1,2),(4,5),\ldots,(19,20)\), on which \(d_0\) acts as \((+1,-1)\);
- 6 free positions \(3,6,\ldots,18\), where \(d_0\) is 0.

Shifting by \(t\) changes a pair \((p,q)\) to \((p+t,q-t)\).
- A pair \((0,0)\) or \((1,1)\) is fixed and allows only \(t=0\).
- A pair \((1,0)\) can become \((0,1)\) with \(t=-1\); a pair \((0,1)\) can become \((1,0)\) with \(t=+1\).

A second preimage therefore exists exactly when at least one pair has sum 1 and all sum-1 pairs have the same orientation, either all \((1,0)\) or all \((0,1)\). In that case the line contains exactly 2 preimages.

**Counting.**
- For a fixed orientation, each pair has 3 options (\(00\), \(11\), or the oriented sum-1 pair), and at least one pair must be the oriented one. That gives \(3^7-2^7=2187-128=2059\) pair configurations.
- With two orientations and \(2^6=64\) choices for the free positions, the number of such \(a\) is \(64\cdot 2\cdot 2059=263552\).
- Each such \(b\) has exactly 2 preimages, so the number of such \(b\) is \(263552/2=131776\).

ANSWER: 131776
